summary: The fix terminates on symlink cycles and returns 'unavailable' for missing, unreadable and cyclic trees with no dangling references, but the new walker has no bound on acyclic symlink fan-out, so a crafted tree can make tree_digest run for minutes.

findings.summary: _collect_records follows every symlinked directory with only an ancestor-chain cycle check and no visited set or work bound, so an acyclic symlink fan-out is walked once per path and grows exponentially with depth.
findings.evidence: ENG-24 (no bound on work for an input-driven walk) and ENG-21 (the walk repeats work). Probe on this worktree (scratchpad sec2/probe.py): a chain of directories where each level holds 2 symlinks to the next level, with one leaf file: depth 10 takes 0.75 s; depth 14 takes 18.56 s. The seam wording 'bounded walk, no hang' is met only for cycles. The prior SEC-3 advisory asked for visited realpaths and a bound; the fix tracks ancestors only. tree_digest runs in write_provenance before launch and in installed_factory, so a symlink-fan-out tree in --from-checkout or the installed skill stalls the driver with no timeout.
findings.fix: Track a visited set of realpaths across the whole walk (a directory already hashed is skipped or recorded 'unavailable'), or cap total entries visited and return 'unavailable' on overflow. Add a test with a 2-way symlink fan-out asserting a bounded result.
